paragraphs.text: Cos amoris amor. Ara amorem illius, saith Bernard. Not to love them that so loved us, is to be worse than a publican, more hard-hearted than a Jew. {Mat 5:46} That the three children burned not in the furnace was a miracle, {Dan 3:25} so it is that men so favoured love not God.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore thou shalt love the Lord.

He speaks unto them as to eye-witncsses; and those that have such evidence and self-experience are usually more affected than those that have things by hearsay only. "Mine eye affects my heart." {Lam 3:51}

i.e., Hath so destroyed and dismayed them, that to this day we hear no more of them: as the Romans so quailed and quelled King Attalus, that he made a law that none of his successors should make war with that state for ever.
paragraphs.anchor: Hath destroyed them unto this day

paragraphs.text: A diary should be diligently kept of what God does for us, {Psa 102:18} for the help of our slippery memories, and the stirring up of our dull hearts to a contention in godliness.
paragraphs.anchor: And what he did unto you.

paragraphs.text: Who were Reubenites; and therefore discontented, say the Jewish doctors, because the birthright was taken from Reuben, for his incest, and given to Judah and Joseph. Korah is here, though not mentioned yet, neither excluded nor excused.
{See Trapp on "Deu 4:40"}
Fetching and carrying water, called therefore the water of their feet, as our life is called, "the life of our hands," {Isa 57:10} because maintained with the labour of our hands.
paragraphs.anchor: And wateredst it with thy foot.

paragraphs.text: God crowning the year with his goodness, and his paths dropping fatness. {Psa 65:10-12} In the Hebrew it is, Thy chariot-wheel tracks; for the clouds are God’s chariots, {Psa 104:3} in which water is bound. {Job 26:8} How they are upheld, and why they fall here and now, we know not, and wonder. The Egyptians used in a profane mockery to tell other nations, that if God should forget to rain, they might chance to starve for it; they thought the rain was of God, but not their river Nile. See Eze 29:3; Eze 29:9 Isa 19:5-6.
paragraphs.anchor: Ver. ll. And drinketh water of the rain of heaven.

paragraphs.text: Rain God gives to all by a providence, {Act 14:17 Job 38:26} but to his Israel by virtue of a promise, whereby they might "live, not as by bread only, but as by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God."
paragraphs.anchor: That I will give you the rain.

paragraphs.text: Having first deceived itself; for "the heart is deceitful above all things," {Jer 17:9} and may say to many, as the heart of Apollonius the tyrant seemed to say to him, who dreamed one night, that he was flayed by the Scythians, and boiled in a caldron, and that his heart spake to him out of the kettle and said, Eγω σοι τουτων αιτια, It is I that have drawn thee to all this. {a} Those in hell cry so.
paragraphs.anchor: That your heart be not deceived.

With the way to either, that if ye miscarry ye may have none to blame but yourselves. For oft it falls out, that whereas "the foolishness of man perverteth his way, his heart fretteth against the Lord." {Pro 19:3}

That is, Pronounce it there. See Jos 8:33. Hence the Samaritans built their temple on this mount as a blessed place, and there worshipped they knew not what {Joh 4:20; Joh 4:22} calling themselves, Those that belong to the blessed mount.
